q1_issues.issue: The capitalized run "Cauldron Hall Warden" is split, the Name atom going only to the substring "Cauldron Hall", where Names and casing treats a capitalized run that exceeds the bare class word ("Warden") as the referent's own name - one opaque symbol, one Name atom, plus an ordinary type atom from the name-internal kind word.

(Possession sk_warden_1 cauldron_hall) asserts a warden-to-hall association that the text conveys only by juxtaposition; it is licensed by the proper-noun-premodifier rule but not if the whole capitalized run is the name.

q2_gaps: a proper-noun premodifier whose common-noun head is itself CAPITALIZED ("the Cauldron Hall Warden"): the premodifier rule's examples all have lowercase heads ("a Northgate spokesman"), while the casing rule states that an adjacent LOWERCASE common noun is not part of a name and that the capitalized run exceeding the bare class word signals name-hood - nothing resolves which rule wins
notes: Everything downstream of the name question conforms: prefer takes Experiencer/Stimulus by the progressive test, deep_ebb_water is a bare-kind filler with genus water and its noun modifier correctly unexposed, and the simple present correctly gets no status atom.
